title: Pathum Thani to Ayutthaya Day Trip: A Full 1-Day Plan | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: An easy one-day trip from Pathum Thani to Ayutthaya, Thailand. Leave Rangsit early, visit the old temples, eat boat noodles, and grab roti sai mai — with real times, fees, and routes.
keywords: Pathum Thani Ayutthaya day trip, Ayutthaya from Rangsit, cross-province day trip Thailand, one day trip Ayutthaya
h1:
Pathum Thani to Ayutthaya
An Old City in One Day
intro: Pathum Thani sits closer to Ayutthaya than most people realize. Leave Rangsit in the morning, drive an hour, and you're on Ayutthaya's island town — visiting the old temples, eating boat noodles, buying roti sai mai to take home, and back at your own place before dark. This is a one-day plan built from a route we actually drove, with real times, entry fees, and meal stops that turned out to land just right.

blocks.html: A lot of Pathum Thani locals skip Ayutthaya because they assume it's an overnight trip. But from Rangsit or downtown Pathum Thani, you hop onto Phahonyothin Road (Highway 1), connect to Highway 32 (the Asia Highway), and you're on Ayutthaya's island town in about 50 minutes to an hour. It's only around 50 kilometers. Go in the morning, come back in the evening, sleep in your own bed — no need to burn several days of leave.

This plan is built for people driving themselves, leaving early and heading back the same evening. It focuses on the old temples clustered on the island town, close enough to move between easily, broken up with a boat-noodle lunch and the local sweet everyone knows, roti sai mai. Going on a weekday is far easier than the weekend, when it's crowded and parking is a pain.

blocks.text: How to Leave Pathum Thani Early Enough

blocks.html: If you're driving, the easiest starting point is the Rangsit intersection or Future Park. Head north on Phahonyothin, pass Wang Noi, then take Highway 32 toward Ayutthaya. Watch for the signs into the town / island town. Between 7 and 8 in the morning traffic is still light. If you leave later, the Wang Noi stretch can get a little sticky — give yourself an extra 15 minutes.

No car of your own? You can still go. There are vans and minibuses on the Rangsit–Ayutthaya line leaving from the Rangsit side, with fares in the low hundreds of baht and a ride of about an hour and a bit. Or take a northern-line train to Ayutthaya station and cross by ferry into the island town, with tickets starting in the tens of baht. But if you want to hit several temples in one day, driving yourself or renting a car is still more flexible, since the temples are spread around the island town.

blocks.title: A Tip for Getting Around the Island Town
blocks.html: If you're not driving, once you reach the island town, rent a bicycle or motorbike by the day around Chao Phrom Market and Naresuan Road. Rentals run in the low hundreds of baht. Cycling between the temples inside the historical park is fun and far easier to park than a car.

blocks.text: The One-Day Plan, Hour by Hour

blocks.html: This plan splits into a morning of temple visits, a midday boat-noodle break, and an afternoon of riverside temples plus souvenirs. Temples that sit close together are grouped into the same block so you're not driving in circles. Entry to the temples inside the historical park is 10 THB per site for Thais and 50 THB for foreigners, or a combined Thai pass for 40 THB that's better value if you're hitting several.

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.title: Onto the Island Town, Visit the Royal Temples

items.activity: Leave Rangsit / downtown Pathum Thani, take Phahonyothin then Highway 32
items.note: Fill up the tank and use the restroom before you head out

items.activity: Arrive at Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon, the first stop just southeast of the island town
items.note: Open 08:00–17:00. You can climb the big chedi, and the white reclining Buddha photographs beautifully in morning light

items.activity: Enter the island town, see Wat Mahathat and the Buddha head wrapped in tree roots
items.note: Open 08:30–16:30. Entry 10 THB for Thais. This is the image of Ayutthaya everyone photographs

items.activity: Walk on to Wat Phra Si Sanphet + Wihan Phra Mongkhon Bophit
items.note: The two sit side by side. The three chedis in a row are the highlight; pay respects to the large Phra Mongkhon Bophit in the hall next door

items.activity: Find a boat-noodle shop around the island town, order several bowls the local way
items.note: Small bowls, bold flavor, salty leading sweet, 15–20 THB a bowl. Ordering 4–5 bowls per person is totally normal

items.activity: Sit down for a coffee, duck out of the afternoon sun for a bit
items.note: Around Naresuan and Pa Thon roads there are several small cafes in old buildings

items.activity: Head to Wat Chaiwatthanaram on the Chao Phraya River, the west side of the island town
items.note: Open 07:30–16:00. The rows of Khmer-style prangs are striking, and it's where a lot of people rent Thai costumes for photos

items.activity: Stop by Wat Lokayasutharam to see the long open-air reclining Buddha
items.note: On the island town, no entry fee, fewer people than the main temples, a calm atmosphere

items.activity: Buy roti sai mai as a souvenir before leaving town
items.note: The well-known shops are near the hospital and along U Thong Road; pick ones that make the wrappers fresh daily, a few tens of baht a pack

items.activity: Get on Highway 32 back to Pathum Thani
items.note: Try to leave before 17:30, since the Wang Noi stretch back toward the city starts to clog up

items.activity: Arrive in Rangsit / Pathum Thani, home before dark
items.note: A one-day trip wrapped up nicely, with no need to find a room

blocks.text: The Temples and Sights We Picked

items.name: Wat Mahathat
items.blurb: An ancient temple on the island town. The highlight is the sandstone Buddha head cradled in the roots of a bodhi tree — the image people picture before anything else when they think of Ayutthaya. You can walk the grounds comfortably in an hour.

items.name: Wat Phra Si Sanphet
items.blurb: The royal temple within the old palace grounds. The three bell-shaped chedis in a row are a symbol of Ayutthaya. It sits right beside Wihan Phra Mongkhon Bophit, so you can walk between the two in one stop.

items.name: Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon
items.blurb: You can climb the big chedi for the view. There's a white reclining Buddha and rows of Buddha images draped in yellow robes. It works well as the first stop in the morning since it sits just outside the island town on the way in.

items.name: Wat Chaiwatthanaram
items.blurb: A temple on the Chao Phraya River with some of the most beautifully arranged Khmer-style prangs anywhere. It's a popular spot to rent Thai costumes for photos, and on some cool-season nights it opens for evening viewing too.

items.name: Wihan Phra Mongkhon Bophit
items.blurb: A large bronze Buddha enshrined in a hall, right next to Wat Phra Si Sanphet. Out front there's a market of food and souvenirs to browse. No entry fee for the hall.
items.meta: Next to Wat Phra Si Sanphet · market out front

items.name: Wat Lokayasutharam
items.blurb: A long open-air reclining Buddha on the island town, with fewer people than the main temples and a calm atmosphere. A good stop in the late afternoon before heading back. No entry fee.
items.meta: On the island town · no entry fee

blocks.text: What to Eat Through the Day

blocks.html: Ayutthaya's signature dish is boat noodles — small bowls with a bold flavor, salty leading and sweet following, at 15–20 THB a bowl, and people order many bowls per meal. Several long-running shops are now into their third generation, scattered around the island town and along the canals. Order both the pork and the beef versions to compare side by side.

items: Boat noodles — the main lunch of the trip. Small, punchy bowls; ordering several is better value than one big bowl, and there's both a pork and a beef recipe

Roti sai mai — the town's signature sweet souvenir, a soft wrapper around fluffy strands of spun sugar. Pick a shop that makes its wrappers fresh daily, and buy it just before you leave since it doesn't keep long
Grilled river prawns — if you have the time and budget, several riverside restaurants serve big river prawns, a heavier meal a lot of people come specifically for
Old-style Thai sweets — around Wihan Phra Mongkhon Bophit there's a market selling Thai treats like khanom buang and foi thong to snack on as you walk

blocks.title: Straight Talk About Sun and Rain
blocks.html: Ayutthaya has a lot of walking out in the open, and the midday sun is intense. Bring a hat, an umbrella, and water. If you go in the rainy season, there may be showers in the afternoon — pack a rain jacket or reorder the plan to keep the indoor temples for later in the day.

blocks.text: Budget Per Person for One Day

items: Fuel + tolls — driving yourself there and back runs about 300–500 THB per car; the more people you split it with, the cheaper
Temple entry — 10 THB per site for Thais, or a 40 THB combined pass good for several sites
Food — boat noodles, coffee, and sweets total around 150–250 THB per person
Roti sai mai souvenirs — a few tens of baht a pack; 2–3 packs comes to around 100 THB
Full-day total — if 3–4 of you drive together, it averages around 300–450 THB each for the whole day

faq.q: How long does it take to get from Pathum Thani to Ayutthaya?
faq.a: Driving yourself from Rangsit or downtown Pathum Thani, taking Phahonyothin then Highway 32, takes about 50 minutes to an hour over roughly 50 kilometers. Leave before 8 in the morning while traffic is still light and you can do it as an easy round-trip day.

faq.q: Can I get to Ayutthaya from Pathum Thani without a car?
faq.a: Yes. There are vans and minibuses on the Rangsit–Ayutthaya line leaving from the Rangsit side, with fares in the low hundreds of baht. Or take a northern-line train to Ayutthaya station and cross by ferry into the island town. Once you're in town, rent a bicycle or motorbike to get around.

faq.q: Is one day enough to see the temples in Ayutthaya?
faq.a: It's enough for the main temples — Wat Mahathat, Wat Phra Si Sanphet, Wihan Phra Mongkhon Bophit, Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon, and Wat Chaiwatthanaram. If you order them so the nearby ones fall in the same block, you won't have to drive in circles and can see them comfortably in a single day.

faq.q: How much is temple entry in Ayutthaya?
faq.a: Temples inside the historical park are 10 THB per site for Thais and 50 THB for foreigners, or a combined Thai pass for 40 THB if you plan to enter several. Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon is free for Thais and 20 THB for foreigners.

faq.q: Should I go on a weekday or a weekend?
faq.a: A weekday is far easier, both for crowds and for parking. Weekends, especially in the cool season, get busy. Wat Chaiwatthanaram and Wat Mahathat are hard to park at and hot. Arrive early to dodge the afternoon sun and the crowds.
